title: Tenant-aware routing and schema enforcement for hosted streaming toolcalls
creator: Lina Zhao
description:
Problem: Multiple enterprise customers have asked for per-tenant control over how streaming chat requests that invoke tools/functions are routed (e.g., low-latency regional nodes vs cost-optimized pool) and for automated validation/enforcement of structured output schemas for toolcall responses. Current hosted runtime supports region routing via account-level config and basic tool calling, but lacks request-scoped policy controls and first-class schema enforcement for streaming responses.

Goal: Deliver a tenant-aware routing policy and schema enforcement layer for hosted streaming toolcalls that allows enterprise customers to: (1) define routing policies at the tenant and request level (priority, preferred region, fallback model variants), (2) apply output schema validators for tool responses with configurable strictness (reject, sanitize, warn), and (3) expose observability and controls in Console for audits and rollouts.

Scope: Design API additions to support request-level routing hints and schema attachments, runtime changes to enforce routing and streaming schema checking, Console UX for policy creation/preview, and SDK updates to pass schema descriptors.

Out of scope: On-prem private deployment packaging and tenant isolation enforcement in Dedicated pools (handled in separate initiative). Non-streaming, single-turn structured output validation will be handled by an adjacent ticket.

Why now: Increasing enterprise demand tied to compliance (structured outputs for downstream parsers), and incidents where customers observed inconsistent tool-call behavior across regions. This feature reduces failed downstream integrations and provides predictable latency SLAs for high-tier customers.
acceptance_criteria: API: Hosted API accepts optional 'routing.hints' and 'output_schema' fields on /v1/chat/stream requests and documents semantics in the OpenAPI spec.
Runtime: Requests with routing.hints are routed to matching capacity pools; fallback behavior matches policy and is logged to tracing.

Schema Enforcement: When output_schema is provided with 'strict:reject', any tool response not matching the schema terminates the stream with a structured error; 'sanitize' attempts best-effort transform and emits telemetry; 'warn' allows response but logs mismatch.
Console: Admins can create tenant policies, preview routing rules, and attach schema templates; policy changes show a dry-run result against sample request history.
SDK: Official JS/py SDKs can attach schema descriptors and surface schema validation errors to callers in streaming mode.
Observability: Dashboard shows per-tenant schema mismatch rate, routing fallback counts, and average tail latency for tenant-scoped routed requests.
Security: Feature passes internal security review and threat model; sensitive info in schemas is redacted in logs by default.
tradeoffs: Strict enforcement increases failed requests for customers with legacy tool behaviors; tradeoff is between safety and friction.
Per-request routing adds policy evaluation overhead on the request path; mitigated via caching of tenant policies and fast-path evaluation.
Maintaining multiple regional pools for strict SLAs increases cost; we'll gate advanced routing to higher tiers to control unit economics.
notes_updates: 2026-02-20 Lina Zhao: Created ticket after consolidated ask from three enterprise customers (finance and healthcare). Initial scoping session with Runtime and Console teams.
2026-02-26 Miguel Santos: Design review completed with Runtime. Agreed to add 'routing.hints' as opt-in to avoid breaking existing clients. Runtime owners flagged caching dependency (ENG-42811).
